nodes.author: Oyindolapo___
nodes.text:
Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV). 
A Thread

Classification and Structure

HMPV belongs to the Pneumoviridae family, which also includes Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). It's a single-stranded, negative-sense RNA virus with a lipid envelope. https://t.co/qdfCa68bI7

nodes.author: Oyindolapo___
nodes.text:
Discovery and Epidemiology

HMPV was first identified in 2001 in the Netherlands. Since then, it has been detected worldwide, with a significant impact on respiratory infections, particularly in children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals.

nodes.author: Oyindolapo___
nodes.text:
Transmission and Clinical Features

HMPV is primarily spread through respiratory droplets, contact with contaminated surfaces, and close contact with infected individuals. The incubation period is approximately 3-7 days.

nodes.author: Oyindolapo___
nodes.text:
Clinical features range from mild to severe and include:

- Upper respiratory tract symptoms (cough, runny nose, sore throat)
- Lower respiratory tract symptoms (bronchiolitis, pneumonia)
- Fever, wheezing, and apnea (in severe cases)

nodes.author: Oyindolapo___
nodes.text: Diagnosis is typically made using molecular tests (PCR) or antigen detection. Treatment is primarily supportive, focusing on relieving symptoms, managing oxygen levels, and preventing complications.

nodes.author: Oyindolapo___
nodes.text:
Prevention and Vaccination

While there is no licensed vaccine against HMPV, several candidates are in various stages of development. Preventative measures include:

- Practicing good hygiene (handwashing, surface cleaning)
- Avoiding close contact with infected individuals

nodes.author: Oyindolapo___
nodes.text: NB: Human Metapneumovirus is an important respiratory pathogen that affects individuals of all ages. Understanding its epidemiology, clinical features, and prevention strategies is crucial for mitigating its impact on public health.
